catalog_quote: 3.3 節では、アクセントの体系について論じる。国頭方言は、音の相対的な高低によって語を弁別するピッチ・アクセント (pitch accent) を持つ。... 国頭方言のアクセント核はもっぱらピッチ上昇によって実現される。... 本節では、高山（2013）にならい、国頭方言は上げ核の有無と位置が弁別的な体系であると考える。 3.3.1. 概論 前述のように、国頭方言は核の有無と位置が弁別的である体系を持つ。すなわち、国頭方言の語は、核を持つもの（hagami「鏡」、futabi「今年」、guzjija「鯨」など）と持たないもの（hjibusji「煙」など）とに分類することが可能である。... 国頭方言における核の位置は、後ろから 1 モーラ目、後ろから 2 モーラ目、後ろから 3 モーラ目のいずれかである。したがって核の有無（あるかないか）と位置（後ろから 1 番目か 2 番目か 3 番目か）とに基づいて、4 種類のアクセント型が区別される。以下、国頭方言の 4 種類のアクセント型をそれぞれ a 型、b 型、c 型、d 型と呼ぶことにする。a 型は核のない型、すなわち無核であり、b 型、c 型、d 型は核のある型、すなわち有核である。... [§3.3.3] a. 核を担う韻律単位はモーラである。b. a 型は核のない型であり、b 型は後ろから 1 モーラ目に、c 型は後ろから 2 モーラ目に、d 型は後ろから 3 モーラ目に核がある型である。ただし b 型は 2 モーラ以上の助詞が後接するとき、核の位置が 1 モーラ右側に移る。c. 核は上げ核であり、核があるモーラの次の韻律単位を上昇させる。

new_statements.quote: These studies have argued that the tonal patterns of Kunigami are lexically contrastive (see §2.6), with distinctions made based on the presence or absence of a raising accent kernel (see §2.3 of Chapter 1, this volume) and, when present, its location within the word. Words lacking a kernel are unaccented (Type A), whereas words with a kernel are accented. ... In Type C words, the kernel is located on the penultimate syllable, whereas in Type D words, it is located on the antepenultimate syllable. ... [Type B:] it is located on the penultimate syllable of the unit formed by one word and one clitic. In the absence of a clitic, the kernel of Type B words is realized on the word-final syllable

new_statements.relation_note: Same author and same analysis type as the catalog record (Yokoyama 2017 diss.: Kunigami has pitch accent with a rising kernel 上げ核 whose presence/absence and position are distinctive; catalog classification tonal). The 2026 chapter agrees on the type (lexical pitch accent realized by pitch rise, unaccented vs accented classes) and adds/updates detail: kernel position stated in syllables from the right edge (penult = Type C, antepenult = Type D, penult of word+clitic = Type B, i.e. word-final in isolation) rather than the diss.'s '1st/2nd/3rd mora from the end' (the chapter argues explicitly that the syllable, not the mora, is the counting unit, Table 13.3 p. 324); four classes A-D; domain =…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kunigami Okinoerabu has a lexical pitch accent (word-tone) system, not stress: words contrast by the presence/absence and location of a 'raising kernel' (L*+H; the syllable after the kernel-bearing syllable is high). Four lexical classes: Type A unaccented (only a non-accentual pitch rise at the end of the bunsetsu); Type B kernel on the penultimate syllable of word+first clitic (word-final, lengthened syllable when no clitic follows); Type C kernel on the penultimate syllable of the lexical word; Type D kernel on the antepenultimate syllable. Two-mora nouns show 3 patterns, three-mora nouns 4. Kernel location is computed right-to-left from the right edge; the counting unit and TBU is the syllable (mora only in a few monosyllabic heavy Type C words like naa 'inside', wui 'bucket', explained diachronically). The domain of tone assignment is argued to be the bunsetsu, with at most one kernel per bunsetsu. The system is obligatory (every word has at least one high-pitched prominence in the bunsetsu) but not culminative (Type C words of 3+ morae surface with two H's, e.g. ⸢fu⸣ta⸢bi 'this year'). In Uwano's typology it is debated whether Kunigami is multipattern or a four-pattern (N-pattern) system. The word 'stress' is not used; prominence is described entirely in terms of pitch/tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None as such (no stress). The chapter describes 'redundant' (predictable) word-initial pitch rises: in Type B all syllables before the kernel syllable are high, in Type C only the word-initial syllable is high (§3.2, p. 329); Type A has a redundant bunsetsu-final rise (§3.3, p. 330). These are non-contrastive and predictable from the kernel position.
new_statements.exceptions: Two-mora words consisting of one heavy syllable (naa 'inside', wui 'bucket') realize the kernel rise within the syllable and require the mora as counting unit/TBU; assigned to Type C and explained as reflexes of proto-Ryukyuan disyllables (*naka, *woke) (pp. 324-325). Type D is argued to be a historical split from Type C conditioned by a close vowel in the penultimate syllable, later extended to recent loans (takako, akemi, tomato, terebi) regardless of vowel height (p. 328). Compounds: A+X -> A; B+B -> B; B+A/C -> C; C+X -> C (16 compounds only, pp. 326-327).
new_statements.identity_note: All data are from the Kunigami variety (easternmost village, Eastern Okinoerabu group) of Okinoerabu, two male speakers born 1945 and 1947; the chapter notes that each of the island's 42 villages has a distinct variety and that Masana (per Matsumori 2000) distinguishes patterns by pitch FALL rather than rise, so the description should be filed under Okinoerabu, Kunigami dialect (as the catalog record already is), not generalized to all Okinoerabu varieties.

sources.quote: p.370: '国頭方言の名詞アクセントは，上げ核の有無と位置が弁別的な多型アクセントである。核を担う単位はモーラであり，アクセントが指定される単位は語である。a 型は無核，b 型は語末から 1 モーラ目，c 型は語末から 2 モーラ目，d 型は語末から 3 モーラ目…' Refinement vs 2017: for 4-mora words a fifth type (e 型, kernel 4th from end) is recognised and some words classed d-type in 2017 are reanalysed via a kernel-shift rule off heavy syllables (fn.4: '横山（2017）では，これらの語を d 型に分類したが…解釈を変更した').
